scenes.tts: Under a microscope, a drop of pond water may show a Paramecium. It is a single cell, shaped like a slipper. This one cell swims, catches food, pumps out extra water, and splits in two. Your body does the same kinds of jobs, with trillions of cells. So how can one cell survive alone?
scenes.visual: A slipper-shaped cell appears; four job chips appear as named; a grid of many small cells for the body; the question.
scenes.narration: Under a microscope, a drop of pond water may show a Paramecium. It is a single cell, shaped like a slipper. scenes.tts: A unicellular organism is a living thing made of one cell. A Paramecium swims with cilia, short hair-like structures that beat together like oars. Food is enclosed in food vacuoles, where it is digested. Water keeps moving in by osmosis. A contractile vacuole, a sac, fills with that extra water and squeezes it out. Last, binary fission: one cell divides into two.
scenes.visual: Large cell: cilia ticks beat, food vacuole fills, water arrows in, contractile vacuole pulses, then the cell pinches into two.

scenes.tts: A multicellular organism is made of many cells. A specialized cell has a structure that suits it to a particular job. Similar cells working together form a tissue, such as muscle. Several tissues form an organ, such as the heart. Related organs form an organ system, such as the circulatory system.
scenes.visual: Row of many cells; one highlighted as specialized; chain cell, tissue, organ, organ system with examples.
scenes.narration: A multicellular organism is made of many cells. A specialized cell has a structure that suits it to a particular job. Similar cells working together form a tissue, such as muscle. Several tissues form an organ, such as the heart. Related organs form an organ system, such as the circulatory system.

scenes.tts: Each specialized cell has a shape that fits its job. A nerve cell has a long extension that carries signals far. Some human nerve cells reach about a metre long. A red blood cell is a small, flexible, dented disc, so it bends through narrow vessels. A root hair cell has a long tube that touches the soil, where water enters.
scenes.visual: Three labelled schematic cells appear one at a time, each with its job.

scenes.tts: Do these cells carry different instructions? Mostly no. Nearly every body cell with a nucleus carries essentially the same D N A. What differs is gene expression, the use of a gene's instructions to make a product, such as a protein. A muscle cell uses the genes for proteins that shorten. A red blood cell in the making uses the genes for hemoglobin. A mature red blood cell is an exception: it has no nucleus.

scenes.tts: So how can one cell survive alone? A Paramecium holds the structures for every job inside its one cell. Your body shares those jobs among specialized cells. Their shapes fit their work. Nearly all carry the same D N A, but each kind uses different genes.
